Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- The failing test invokes DefaultParser.parse with a single long option token: "--prefix". The test expects that an exact long option name matches without ambiguity.

- Parsing flow:
  - DefaultParser.parse(...) delegates to handleToken (lines 221-254), which routes tokens starting with "--" to handleLongOption (lines 367-377).
  - Since the token has no '=', handleLongOptionWithoutEqual is used (lines 389-404).

- Ambiguity arises in handleLongOptionWithoutEqual:
  - It calls options.getMatchingOptions(token) (line 391) to find matching long options.
  - If multiple matches are found, it throws AmbiguousOptionException (lines 396-399).

- Root cause in Options.getMatchingOptions(String opt) (lines 233-250):
  - The method strips leading hyphens (line 235) and then collects all long option names that start with the provided opt (lines 241-247).
  - Critically, it does not prioritize an exact match. The method’s comment “for a perfect match return the single option only” (line 239) is not implemented; it always adds any long option starting with opt.
  - Thus, when an exact long option exists (e.g., "prefix") alongside another option with the same prefix (e.g., "prefixSomething"), getMatchingOptions returns both, leading handleLongOptionWithoutEqual to treat the token as ambiguous and throw AmbiguousOptionException.

- This explains both:
  - The test failure for "--prefix" (exact match should be accepted but is treated as ambiguous).
  - The bug report case where "--import=FILE" becomes ambiguous between "import" and "importToOpen" in 1.3, whereas 1.2 accepted the exact match. The same logic applies in handleLongOptionWithEqual (lines 416-448), which also uses getMatchingOptions and throws AmbiguousOptionException on multiple matches (lines 424-432).

Conclusion:
- The bug is caused by Options.getMatchingOptions not returning only the exact match when one exists. This causes DefaultParser to see multiple matches and throw AmbiguousOptionException even for exact long option names, breaking expected behavior.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
